extracted.intended_audience: comedians, humor writers, and students of humor theory
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Eastman's play theory to produce humor by establishing a play/frame of disinterestedness, signaling artifice, staging a clear disappointment, and ensuring the audience experiences joy rather than distress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be in fun (Law 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience must be in a playful state of mind before the comic stimulus arrives; the comedian's first job is to put them in fun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the audience is earnest, no joke will land. Techniques to establish 'fun' include preambles, playful tone, rapport-building, staging, and contextual cues. Anti-pattern: attempting humor when the audience's frame is serious (e.g., at a funeral) will fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey a sense of artifice or play (Law 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The humorous material itself must signal 'this is play' so the audience understands it is not a sincere proposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signal play through tone, pacing, exaggeration, stylization, or other markers of artifice. The speaker must make clear the content is playful rather than earnest. Anti-pattern: presenting a serious proposition without markers of play — this defeats the comic frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the disappointment plain (Law 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comic event must clearly involve a disappointment — a frustration of expectation, a fall from dignity, or a thwarting of desire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy requires an identifiable disappointment as the comic substance; without it there is nothing to be framed as play. Ensure the audience can perceive what expectation was frustrated or what fall occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the disappointment joyous (Law 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disappointment must be presented so that it produces enjoyment rather than distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achieve joyous disappointment via the right pace, appropriate surrounding affect, triviality or lightness of stakes, and signals that the disappointment is contained. Anti-patterns: pacing or framing that evokes pity, anger, or real distress rather than amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinterested attitude (audience releases genuine investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor depends on the audience adopting a temporary disinterestedness — they must not be genuinely invested in the outcome or harmed by the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the hero falls but we 'don't really care'; institutions mocked in the moment; mock aggression is funnier than real aggression. If the audience cares too much (high stakes or personal involvement), the play frame collapses and humor fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup must reinforce the play frame
rubrics_metrics.description: The setup should actively establish/play up the playful frame through stylistic choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use light tone, exaggeration, and stylization in the setup so the audience is primed to interpret what follows as play. The setup's job is to reduce real-world investment and cue amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a real, identifiable disappointment/negative event
rubrics_metrics.description: A genuine negative event or thwarted expectation must occur in the material for comic substance to exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on bland or neutral content; the comic kernel is the disappointment itself. However, ensure the disappointment is presented within the play frame so it yields amusement rather than distress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep audience interest light or removed (manage stakes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience's normal serious interest must be suspended: stakes should be trivial or presented so the audience can hold them lightly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques include minimizing consequences, using parody/exaggeration, or signaling containment. Anti-pattern: real disasters or matters affecting people the audience cares about — these maintain serious interest and kill the play frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure joy is the audience's actual response (not pity, anger, or shock)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intended affective outcome of the comic event must be enjoyment rather than negative affects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the framing, pace, and signals produce laughter/joy. If the response is pity, outrage, or shock, adjust framing (more artifice, lower stakes, clearer containment) until joy predominates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid content that defeats the play frame (exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude serious propositions presented sincerely, real disasters affecting people we care about, and trivial bland content with no disappointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories either lack the play signal or engage the audience's real interest; they therefore fail Eastman's criteria for humor. Use this as a checklist of material to avoid or reframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic checklist (evaluation questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short evaluative checklist to test whether material meets the play-theory conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: Is the audience in fun? Has the speaker put them there? Does the material itself signal 'this is play'? Is there an identifiable disappointment/fall/frustration? Is the disappointment small enough or framed playfully enough that the response is joyous rather than distressing? Has the audience's normal serious interest been suspended?
